And.name: Andromeda
And.lore: The Chained Maiden, home to the Andromeda Galaxy (M31).

Ant.name: Antlia
Ant.lore: The Air Pump, invented by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 18th century.

Aps.name: Apus
Aps.lore: The Bird of Paradise, representing an exotic tropical bird.

Aqr.name: Aquarius
Aqr.lore: The Water Bearer, one of the oldest recognized constellations.

Aql.name: Aquila
Aql.lore: The Eagle that carried Zeus's thunderbolts in Greek mythology.

Ara.name: Ara
Ara.lore: The Altar where the Olympian gods made offerings before battling the Titans.

Ari.name: Aries
Ari.lore: The Ram whose Golden Fleece became the quest of Jason and the Argonauts.

Aur.name: Auriga
Aur.lore: The Charioteer, containing the bright golden star Capella.

Boo.name: Boötes
Boo.lore: The Herdsman or Bear Driver, following the Great Bear around the pole.

Cae.name: Caelum
Cae.lore: The Chisel, introduced by Lacaille to represent an engraver's tool.

Cam.name: Camelopardalis
Cam.lore: The Giraffe, a faint northern constellation introduced in 1612.

Cnc.name: Cancer
Cnc.lore: The Crab that pinched Heracles during his fight with the Hydra.

CVn.name: Canes Venatici
CVn.lore: The Hunting Dogs Asterion and Chara, held on a leash by Bootes.

CMa.name: Canis Major
CMa.lore: The Greater Dog, faithful hound of Orion, containing Sirius the Dog Star.

CMi.name: Canis Minor
CMi.lore: The Lesser Dog, containing the brilliant star Procyon.

Cap.name: Capricornus
Cap.lore: The Sea Goat, a mythological hybrid creature of goat and fish.

Car.name: Carina
Car.lore: The Keel of the legendary ship Argo Navis that sailed for the Golden Fleece.

art.note: Historically part of Argo Navis (Keel). Mapped to carina.png (and argonavis.png).

Cas.name: Cassiopeia
Cas.lore: The Queen of Ethiopia, vanity-cursed to circle the celestial pole forever.

Cen.name: Centaurus
Cen.lore: The Centaur, representing Chiron the wisest and most just of centaurs.

Cep.name: Cepheus
Cep.lore: The King of Ethiopia, husband of Cassiopeia and father of Andromeda.

Cet.name: Cetus
Cet.lore: The Sea Monster sent by Poseidon to ravage the Ethiopian coast.

Cha.name: Chamaeleon
Cha.lore: The Chameleon, navigating the faint southern skies.

Col.name: Columba
Col.lore: Noah's Dove, introduced by Petrus Plancius in the late 16th century.

Com.name: Coma Berenices
Com.lore: Berenice's Hair, dedicated to Queen Berenice II of Egypt.

CrA.name: Corona Austrina
CrA.lore: The Southern Crown, a wreath worn by Sagittarius or Centaurus.

art.note: Corona Austrina mapped to corona_austrina.png (canonical corona_australis.png).

CrB.name: Corona Borealis
CrB.lore: The Northern Crown, the jeweled crown of Ariadne given by Dionysus.

Crv.name: Corvus
Crv.lore: The Crow or Raven sent by Apollo to fetch water.

Crt.name: Crater
Crt.lore: The Cup of Apollo, placed beside the celestial Raven.

Cru.name: Crux
Cru.lore: The Southern Cross, the most famous navigational landmark of the Southern Hemisphere.

Cyg.name: Cygnus
Cyg.lore: The Swan flying down the Milky Way, containing the Northern Cross.

Del.name: Delphinus
Del.lore: The Dolphin that carried the Greek poet Arion safely ashore.

Dor.name: Dorado
Dor.lore: The Dolphinfish (Mahi-mahi) or Swordfish of the southern sky.

Dra.name: Draco
Dra.lore: The Dragon Ladon guarding the golden apples in the Garden of the Hesperides.

Equ.name: Equuleus
Equ.lore: The Little Horse, associated with Celeris, foal of Pegasus.

Eri.name: Eridanus
Eri.lore: The celestial River Eridanus where Phaethon fell in myth.

For.name: Fornax
For.lore: The Chemical Furnace, honoring Antoine Lavoisier's laboratory.

Gem.name: Gemini
Gem.lore: The Gemini Twins, Castor and Pollux, immortalized side by side.

Gru.name: Grus
Gru.lore: The Crane, introduced by Dutch navigators Keyser and de Houtman.

Her.name: Hercules
Her.lore: Heracles the legendary hero kneeling after completing his twelve labors.

Hor.name: Horologium
Hor.lore: The Pendulum Clock, commemorating Christiaan Huygens's invention.

art.note: Horologium mapped to horologium.png (original file horlogium.png).

Hya.name: Hydra
Hya.lore: The Water Monster Hydra, the largest of all 88 modern constellations.

Hyi.name: Hydrus
Hyi.lore: The Lesser Water Snake of the deep southern polar sky.

Ind.name: Indus
Ind.lore: The Indian, depicting an indigenous inhabitant of the Americas or Indies.

Lac.name: Lacerta
Lac.lore: The Lizard, introduced by Johannes Hevelius in 1687.

Leo.name: Leo
Leo.lore: The Nemean Lion slain by Heracles in his first labor.

LMi.name: Leo Minor
LMi.lore: The Lesser Lion, introduced by Hevelius between Leo and Ursa Major.

Lep.name: Lepus
Lep.lore: The Hare crouching at the feet of Orion the hunter.

Lib.name: Libra
Lib.lore: The Scales of Justice held by Astraea (Virgo).

Lup.name: Lupus
Lup.lore: The Wolf impaled on the spear of the Centaur.

Lyn.name: Lynx
Lyn.lore: The Lynx, named because only a lynx-eyed observer could spot its faint stars.

Lyr.name: Lyra
Lyr.lore: The Lyre of Orpheus, whose music could charm beasts and trees.

Men.name: Mensa
Men.lore: Table Mountain at Cape Town, South Africa, honored by Lacaille.

Mic.name: Microscopium
Mic.lore: The Microscope, celebrating scientific instruments of the Enlightenment.

Mon.name: Monoceros
Mon.lore: The Unicorn, galloping silently through the winter Milky Way.

Mus.name: Musca
Mus.lore: The Fly, hovering near the Southern Cross.

Oct.name: Octans
Oct.lore: The Octant, containing the South Celestial Pole.

Oph.name: Ophiuchus
Oph.lore: The Serpent Bearer, Asclepius the mythical founder of medicine.

Ori.name: Orion
Ori.lore: Orion the mighty Hunter, one of the most magnificent constellations in the heavens.

Pav.name: Pavo
Pav.lore: The Peacock, sacred bird of Hera in Greek myth.

Peg.name: Pegasus
Peg.lore: Pegasus the Winged Divine Stallion born from the neck of Medusa.

Per.name: Perseus
Per.lore: Perseus the slayer of Medusa and rescuer of Andromeda.

Phe.name: Phoenix
Phe.lore: The mythical Phoenix rising reborn from its own ashes.

Pic.name: Pictor
Pic.lore: The Painter's Easel, another instrument of the arts celebrated by Lacaille.

Psc.name: Pisces
Psc.lore: The Two Fishes tied together by a ribbon, representing Aphrodite and Eros.

PsA.name: Piscis Austrinus
PsA.lore: The Southern Fish drinking the water poured by Aquarius.

Pup.name: Puppis
Pup.lore: The Poop Deck or Stern of the legendary ship Argo Navis.

art.note: Historically part of Argo Navis (Poop Deck). Mapped to puppis.png (and argonavis.png).

Pyx.name: Pyxis
Pyx.lore: The Mariner's Magnetic Compass on board Argo Navis.

Ret.name: Reticulum
Ret.lore: The Reticle, the crosshairs in an astronomical telescope.

Sge.name: Sagitta
Sge.lore: The celestial Arrow shot by Heracles or Apollo.

Sgr.name: Sagittarius
Sgr.lore: The Archer Centaur aiming his bow at the heart of the Scorpion.

Sco.name: Scorpius
Sco.lore: The Scorpion whose venomous sting brought down Orion.

Scl.name: Sculptor
Scl.lore: The Sculptor's Studio, containing the South Galactic Pole.

Sct.name: Scutum
Sct.lore: The Shield of Sobieski, celebrating Polish King John III Sobieski.

Ser.name: Serpens Cauda
Ser.lore: The Serpent held in two halves (Caput and Cauda) by Ophiuchus.

Sex.name: Sextans
Sex.lore: The Astronomical Sextant used by Johannes Hevelius.

Tau.name: Taurus
Tau.lore: The Bull containing the Pleiades and Hyades star clusters.

Tel.name: Telescopium
Tel.lore: The Refracting Telescope invented in the 17th century.

Tri.name: Triangulum
Tri.lore: The Northern Triangle, an ancient geometric constellation.

TrA.name: Triangulum Australe
TrA.lore: The Southern Triangle, mapped by early European explorers.

Tuc.name: Tucana
Tuc.lore: The Toucan, home to the Small Magellanic Cloud.

UMa.name: Ursa Major
UMa.lore: The Great Bear containing the famous Big Dipper / Plough asterism.

UMi.name: Ursa Minor
UMi.lore: The Little Bear containing Polaris the North Star.

Vel.name: Vela
Vel.lore: The Sails of the legendary ship Argo Navis.

art.note: Historically part of Argo Navis (Sails). Mapped to vela.png (and argonavis.png).

Vir.name: Virgo
Vir.lore: The Maiden of Justice (Astraea or Demeter) carrying an ear of wheat.

Vol.name: Volans
Vol.lore: The Flying Fish, skimming above the southern waters.

Vul.name: Vulpecula
Vul.lore: The Fox carrying a goose in its jaws, introduced by Hevelius.
